newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour to insist on Cullen as finance minister.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour to insist on Cullen as finance minister.

text.p: New Zealand Labour Party leader Helen Clark said on Tuesday her party would insist on finance spokesman Michael Cullen becoming finance minister in a Labour-led coalition after Saturday's general election.
"Dr Cullen must be the finance minister. There is no other contender," Clark told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
Clark declined to be drawn on what portfolio might go to Winston Peters, leader of the economic nationalist New Zealand First party, if it entered a coalition with Labour.
"Prime ministers don't speculate on portfolio allocations before an election. But clearly if Mr Peters agrees to come into the government, he must have a portfolio," she said.
Clark would not say if Peters was likely to be deputy prime minister in such an arrangement.
"What's important is that Labour is clearly in the driving seat of the new government, that I am the prime minister and that Dr Cullen is the minister of finance," she said.
